initial: Use case: identity-preserve game sprite animation supplement. Create a 4-column by 3-row contact sheet of twelve FULL BODY poses of the exact IRON THRALL in the first image. The first image is the approved character design and existing paint treatment; the second image is Giovanni da Modena Inferno, the mandatory overall fresco style reference. Continue the SAME thin damned iron-clad servant, not a new knight: same pointed rust-red hood over small iron brow plate, same long pale anguished open-mouthed face, spindly exposed rusty red hands and long fingers, same battered dark grey plate shoulders and segmented limbs, muted red shredded cloth. Keep proportions and body paint consistent with reference 1. No weapons, no magic, no extra spikes or ornaments. Coarse matte painted planes and sparse brown contour; NO increased detail density, tiny metal scratches, shiny highlights, realistic skin, digital gradients, plastic 3D rendering, or blur. This is a small sprite viewed at game size. Broad muted ochre and umber modelling, warm dark grey iron, dim vermilion rags, ivory face. Each cell a square, with clear empty gutters, consistent scale (standing body about 85% cell height), whole fingers and feet inside cell, virtual floor at 93% cell height. Crouched poses naturally lower their head, do not enlarge them to fill the cell. All figures face the viewer in a readable shallow three-quarter view. Background perfectly uniform solid #FF00FF chroma key, NO shadows, scenery, lines, labels or text. Layout poses left to right top to bottom: 1 heavy horizontal cleave gathering, hips coiled and striking arm drawn well to the side; 2 cleave at final held tension, body twisted further, elbow and claw distinctly raised sideways; 3 horizontal cleave crossing in front of the chest, wide readable arm sweep; 4 cleave follow-through, shoulders low and striking arm extended across to opposite side; 5 shoulder-charge brace, deep knees, lowered leading iron shoulder with both hands pulled close, eyes looking forward under hood; 6 charge driving step, same lowered shoulder and left leg driving, whole body leaning forward from hips; 7 next charge running step, right leg drives, same shoulder silhouette and body proportions; 8 heavy braking pivot, feet wide, hips turn and upper body looks back over shoulder, visibly replanting weight; 9 floor-slam preparation, both iron forearms raised high over head with clenched bony hands, knees bent; 10 floor-slam contact, both hands driven down to the virtual floor, deeply crouched, head bowed but face identifiable; 11 floor-slam recovery, lifting torso halfway and drawing hands back from floor, knees still bent; 12 backward elbow strike, looking over shoulder while sweeping elbow back and outward, visibly different from forward claw. These are weighty physical gestures of a damned servant imprisoned in armour, not heroic poses. Preserve the reference character's fearful elongated face, modest plate construction, thin limbs and brushwork.
edit: Edit the FIRST image, the twelve-pose 4-column 3-row Iron Thrall animation sheet. SECOND image is the approved original Iron Thrall and THIRD is the mandatory Giovanni da Modena Inferno fresco reference. Preserve the twelve poses, layout, whole-body scale, foot locations, empty gutters and flat #FF00FF background. Correct the paint treatment to match reference two exactly: remove the continuous golden edging around the plate segments and the polished modelling; iron is dark warm grey, matte and broadly painted, with just a few ochre chips rather than luminous outlines. Use restrained irregular mineral pigment, fine sparse dark brown contours and broad brush planes, the same modest level of detail as the old sheet. Do not add scratches or tiny texture. Reduce the toy-like smooth rounded modelling of limbs; preserve the slender bony character and its original anguished long face rather than making a bulky heroic knight. No blur, no glow, no new objects. One pose correction in cell 12 (last cell): this is a BACKWARD ELBOW strike, so turn the ribcage partly away from the viewer, head looking back over shoulder, elbow protruding toward the viewer while fist stays by ribs, with a planted wide stance. It must visibly differ from the raised claw in cell 2. Everything else remains registered in the same cells.
technical_processing: Chroma-key alpha: min(R,B)-G > 0.24. Remove magenta spill: R := R-max(0,B-G), B := min(B,G). Transparent RGB #553c2e. No resampling, sharpening or painting.

forward_claw.prompt: Game sprite animation supplement: create THREE full-body frames in one horizontal row, equal square cells, flat solid #FF00FF key background. Reference 1 is the exact approved Iron Thrall design and paint; reference 2 is the newest modest-detail animation sheet; reference 3 Giovanni da Modena Inferno is mandatory style. Preserve the thin tormented servant in dark matte grey segmented iron, pointed rust red hood, long anguished ivory face, ragged vermilion cloth and bony hands. Same proportions and coarse broad painted planes as reference 2; do NOT add detail, metal shine, etched decoration, spikes, weapons or magical glow. Whole figures and all fingers/feet fully inside each cell with gutters, standing feet on same virtual floor at 94% cell height. These THREE frames form ONE short forward claw attack: (1) shoulder and elbow drawn back, claw poised beside the RIGHT side of the chest as viewed on page, knees bent, preparing a short diagonal rake; (2) IMPACT FRAME, same claw thrust FORWARD STRAIGHT AT VIEWER with the PALM EXACTLY AT THE HORIZONTAL CENTRE OF ITS CELL, directly in front of sternum at waist/chest height, readable bent fingers and modest foreshortening, opposite hand held by hip; (3) follow-through: striking arm crossed DOWN and to the LEFT of its own abdomen as viewed on page, palm at about 35 percent cell width, body slightly bowed, elbow across ribs. The critical animation is the SAME HAND moving from RIGHT of body, through CENTRE in frame 2, to LEFT in frame 3; these must not be three identical hands pointing to the right. Keep face recognizable, lean build, matte medieval fresco treatment, not glossy realistic painting. No shadows, floor, labels, text, background scenery, extra hands or extra characters.
